subject: Re: Rerank model fit validation / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Evans <john.evans@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: rerank validation + next steps

Hi John / Anna —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of today's call:
- Goal: improve relevance for ACME Search results (homepage and product search) using a learned reranking layer while preserving latency SLAs.
- Current baseline: BM25 + production heuristic ranker.
- ACME success metrics: downstream CTR / add-to-cart, MRR on relevance judgments, and NDCG@10 for offline evals.

Redwood preliminary recommendations (based on the samples you shared):
- Candidate model(s) to evaluate: "llama2-13b-retrieval-rerank" (quantized int8) and "open-rerank-v1" (smaller, faster baseline).
- Eval setup we used: heldout labeled set (5k queries / judgments), utility weight on first-click; scoring via NDCG@10 and MRR.
- Preliminary improvements observed on your sample (see attached report): NDCG@10 +6.4 pts, MRR +7.2 pts vs your BM25 baseline. Full numbers and breakdown in the attached ndcg_mrr_report_acme_20260315.pdf.

Requested next steps from ACME:
1) Confirm permission for Redwood to run the full eval on the 50k labeled dataset you mentioned (S3 location you shared).
2) Share any latency/infra constraints for the reranker in production (p95 latency target, CPU/GPU placement).
3) Approve a 2-week A/B pilot: 20% traffic, primary metrics NDCG offline, online CTR, latency, and error rate.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt set + eval queries), ndcg_mrr_report_acme_20260315.pdf (prelim results).

Links: evaluation folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-rerank-evals
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-RR1

If that sounds good I'll start the full run and loop in our infra/ops folks to estimate expected latency on your requested instance types.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--

From: John Evans <john.evans@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lee <anna.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: rerank validation + next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we proceed: 

1) Security & compliance: we need the eval to run in our S3 (we will provide a short-term role with read access). Any log/data export from Redwood during the eval needs to be disabled by default — can your team run the eval inside our environment (or a private Redwood runner)?

2) Latency targets: p95 < 120ms for the reranker when serving combined with our backend; typical query size ~ 64 tokens. If quantized 13B meets this that's great, otherwise we need a fallback to smaller model.

3) Can you share the exact NDCG / MRR numbers and a short breakdown by query bucket (head/tail) so our data science team can validate?

4) Timeline: ACME legal will need a short SOW addendum for the pilot. We can get that started once we see the final evaluation metrics.

I'll DM you the S3 path and an IAM role in the next hour.

- John
Head of Search, ACME Corp
john.evans@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Evans <john.evans@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: rerank validation + next steps

John — thanks, appreciate the quick reply. Short answers and the detailed numbers below.

Security & infra:
- We can run the eval inside your environment using a private runner; we will not export logs by default. David can share the minimal steps for infra access.

Latency / model selection:
- In our profiling on a similar 64-token workload on an NVIDIA A10G, quantized llama2-13b-retrieval-rerank averages p95 ~ 110ms with batching disabled; with batching enabled p95 can rise but throughput improves. The smaller open-rerank-v1 is ~45-60ms p95. We recommend a canary that starts with the smaller model and falls back to the 13b variant for complex queries.

Evaluation numbers (prelim; on your 5k heldout sample):
- Baseline (BM25 + heuristic): NDCG@10 = 0.412, MRR = 0.223
- open-rerank-v1: NDCG@10 = 0.451, MRR = 0.261
- llama2-13b-retrieval-rerank (int8): NDCG@10 = 0.476, MRR = 0.295

Breakdown by query bucket (head / mid / tail) — NDCG@10 delta vs baseline:
- head (top 20% queries): +3.1 pts
- mid (next 50%): +6.8 pts
- tail (bottom 30%): +9.6 pts

Notes on evaluation:
- 5k queries, labels provided by ACME DS; ranking evaluator used bias correction for position; metrics computed with the same loss weighting your team provided. Full scripts and exact seed are in the Drive folder.

Proposed A/B plan:
- Duration: 2 weeks
- Traffic split: 20% treatment, 80% control (randomized by user id)
- Treatment: start with open-rerank-v1 for the first day (safety), then switch to llama2-13b-retrieval-rerank if latency is acceptable.
- Metrics to monitor: online CTR, add-to-cart rate, NDCG (offline re-eval on daily labeled sample), p95 latency, error rate, model cost delta.
- Rollback policy: automated rollback to control if CTR drops by >2% or latency p95 exceeds 150ms.

Next steps I need from ACME to start the full eval:
1) S3 read access to the 50k labeled dataset (IAM role or presigned URLs).
2) Confirmation on pilot SOW scope and point of contact for legal.
3) A list of 5-10 priority queries for a quick smoke test in prod canary.

Attaching the same report and prompt set for reference. Let us know if you want a short walkthrough for your DS team — happy to schedule a 30-min session.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, John Evans <john.evans@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: rerank validation + next steps

Looping in a couple technical notes from the runtime side so expectations are clear: 

1) Latency tradeoffs and mitigations:
- Quantized 13B gives the best relevance uplift but will increase cost and p95 vs the smaller model. If ACME needs p95 headroom we recommend: a) int8 quantization + kernel tuning, b) 1-request batching with KV cache pinned for repeated session queries, c) route small queries to open-rerank-v1.

2) Monitoring / telemetry plan for the A/B:
- We'll push per-request token counts, model_id, and upstream latency to the console (masked PII). Offline we will compute daily NDCG on a stratified sample of requests.

3) Metrics we recommend tracking in addition to CTR / add-to-cart: MRR, NDCG@1/5/10, latency p50/p95/p99, and model cost per 1k requests. We will provide a shared dashboard for these.

4) Quick sanity numbers from the validation run (same numbers Marissa shared) plus an additional per-query bucket MRR delta vs baseline:
- Baseline MRR = 0.223
- open-rerank-v1 MRR = 0.261 (+0.038)
- llama2-13b-retrieval-rerank MRR = 0.295 (+0.072)

Next operational steps (internal -> external): we can provision a private runner in ACME's VPC and start the full 50k eval as soon as we receive the IAM role. I'll create the infra ticket and share the runner details and SSM access in the HubSpot deal. 

Marissa / Dev: happy to join the kickoff with ACME infra and DS this week.

-David
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
